questions.question: With which country did India secure a $131 million deal in May 2025 to acquire 'HawkEye 360’s cutting-edge surveillance technology to advance its maritime defense infrastructure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, India secured a deal worth about **$131 million** with the **United States of America** to acquire advanced **HawkEye 360 surveillance technology**.
 
• **HawkEye 360** is a U.S.-based company that specializes in **radio frequency (RF) geospatial intelligence** using satellite constellations.
 
• The technology helps detect and track **radio frequency signals** emitted by ships, communication devices, and radar systems even when vessels attempt to hide their location.
 
• The system strengthens India’s **maritime domain awareness** and supports monitoring of the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• This acquisition contributes to enhancing India’s **maritime defense infrastructure**, improving surveillance against threats such as **illegal fishing**, **smuggling**, and **unauthorized naval activity**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct option is 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HawkEye 360**

 
 
• A **U.S.-based satellite analytics company** headquartered in **Virginia**.
 
• Uses clusters of satellites to collect **radio frequency (RF) data** from across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA)**
 
 
• Refers to the effective understanding of all activities occurring in the **maritime environment**.
 
• Important for monitoring **shipping routes**, **naval operations**, and **illegal maritime activities**.
 
 
 
• **India–US Defence Cooperation**
 
 
• India and the United States have strengthened defence ties through agreements such as **LEMOA**, **COMCASA**, and **BECA**.
 
• These agreements facilitate **logistics support**, **secure communications**, and **geospatial intelligence sharing**.

questions.question: Which state High Court in January 2025 has mandated that individuals in live-in relationships must sign a legal contract outlining financial responsibilities and childcare provisions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

__
 
• In **January 2025**, the **Rajasthan High Court** directed that couples living in **live-in relationships** should sign a **legal contract** specifying their responsibilities.
 
• The suggested agreement should clearly mention **financial responsibilities**, **maintenance obligations**, and **childcare provisions**.
 
• The court observed that such contracts could help prevent **future disputes** between partners and provide legal clarity regarding rights and duties.
 
• The direction was made during hearings involving petitions filed by couples seeking **police protection** for their live-in relationship.
 
• The observation aimed to safeguard the interests of partners, particularly regarding **financial security** and **responsibility towards children**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct option is 3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal Status of Live-in Relationships in India**

 
 
• Live-in relationships are not illegal and have been recognised by the **Supreme Court of India** in several judgments.
 
• They are considered part of the **right to life and personal liberty under Article 21** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Protection under Law**
 
 
• Women in live-in relationships are protected under the **Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005**.
 
• Children born from such relationships are considered **legitimate** under Indian law.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Court’s Observation**
 
 
• To establish **legal clarity** in live-in relationships.
 
• To ensure proper arrangements for **financial obligations** and **child welfare**.

questions.question: Which two national parks achieved the highest scores of 92.97% in the Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) 2020–2025 of National Parks and Protected Areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eravikulam and Dachigam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE)** is an important framework developed by the Indian government to assess the performance of **National Parks and Protected Areas**.
 
• In the **MEE 2020–2025**, the national parks of **Eravikulam** (located in Kerala) and **Dachigam** (located in Jammu & Kashmir) achieved the **highest scores of 92.97%**, reflecting their exceptional management and conservation efforts.
 
• The evaluation process considers various parameters like biodiversity conservation, resource management, community participation, and sustainable tourism practices.
 
• **Eravikulam National Park** is renowned for protecting the **Nilgiri Tahr**, an endangered mountain goat, and its unique montane grassland ecosystem.
 
• **Dachigam National Park** is famous for its conservation of the **Kashmir Stag (Hangul)**, which is critically endangered, and its pristine Himalayan landscapes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE):**

 
 
• The MEE framework is globally recognized and implemented in India by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• It evaluates the effectiveness of management in protected areas and ensures they meet conservation and biodiversity goals.
 
• The evaluation employs parameters such as **context, planning, inputs, processes, outputs, and outcomes**.
 
• The results are used to improve the management strategies of protected areas and ensure sustainable conservation practices.
 
 
 
• **Eravikulam National Park:**
 
 
• Located in the **Idukki District of Kerala**, it was established in **1978**.
 
• It is home to the **Nilgiri Tahr**, which is endemic to the Western Ghats.
 
• The park is also famous for the **Kurinji flower**, which blooms once every 12 years.
 
• It encompasses unique grasslands and shola forests, supporting a wide variety of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Dachigam National Park:**
 
 
• Located near **Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir**, it was declared a national park in **1981**.
 
• It is the last stronghold of the critically endangered **Kashmir Stag (Hangul)**.
 
• The park is characterized by its alpine meadows, coniferous forests, and rugged mountainous terrain.
 
• It also provides habitat for species such as Himalayan black bears, leopards, and various bird species.
 
 
 
• **Importance of National Parks:**
 
 
• National parks play a critical role in **biodiversity conservation** by protecting flora, fauna, and their ecosystems.
 
• They help in **climate regulation** by acting as carbon sinks and preserving water resources.
 
• They promote **ecotourism** and foster local community livelihoods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of other options:**

 
 
• **Gir and Kaziranga:** While Gir is known for the Asiatic Lion and Kaziranga for the one-horned rhinoceros, they did not achieve the highest MEE score.
 
• **Periyar and Sundarbans:** Periyar in Kerala and Sundarbans in West Bengal are significant for tiger reserves, but neither ranked highest in the MEE.
 
• **Bandipur and Kanha:** Both are renowned tiger reserves but did not achieve the top score in the 2020–2025 MEE.

questions.question: Indicating a strong push toward sustainable energy development, the installed renewable energy generating capacity in India increased from 64.04 watts per capita in 2014-15 to what level per capita in 2024-25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**156.31 watts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's **installed renewable energy generating capacity** has seen a significant increase from **64.04 watts per capita** in **2014-15** to **156.31 watts per capita** in **2024-25**, indicating a strong push toward sustainable energy development.
 
• This growth aligns with India's commitment to achieve **450 GW of renewable energy capacity** by **2030**, as part of its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC)** under the Paris Agreement.
 
• The transition has been driven by initiatives like the **National Solar Mission**, **National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy**, and **Green Energy Corridor Project**, which aim to enhance renewable energy adoption and infrastructure.
 
• India has become one of the largest producers of renewable energy globally, leveraging resources such as **solar power, wind energy, hydropower**, and **biomass energy**.
 
• Among the renewable sources, **solar energy** has seen the most rapid growth, with India emerging as the **fourth largest solar power producer** in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Solar Mission:**

 
 
• Launched in **2010**, it aims to achieve **100 GW of solar power** capacity by **2022**.
 
• India has developed large-scale solar parks like the **Bhadla Solar Park** in Rajasthan, which is one of the world's largest solar parks.
 
• The mission also promotes decentralized solar applications such as rooftop solar systems and off-grid solar solutions.
 
 
 
• **Green Energy Corridor Project:**
 
 
• This project facilitates the integration of renewable energy into the grid by strengthening transmission infrastructure.
 
• It covers states with high renewable energy potential like **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka**.
 
• The project is supported by financing from international organizations like the **Asian Development Bank** and **KfW Development Bank**.
 
 
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Commitments:**
 
 
• India committed to achieving **50% of its energy requirements** from renewable sources by **2030** during the **COP26 summit** in Glasgow.
 
• The country aims to reduce its carbon intensity by **33%-35%** by 2030, compared to 2005 levels.
 
 
 
• **Global Renewable Energy Status:**
 
 
• India ranks **fourth globally** in installed renewable energy capacity, following **China, the USA, and Germany**.
 
• Globally, renewable energy accounts for over **30% of electricity generation**, with solar and wind leading the charge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paris Agreement:**

 
 
• India's renewable energy targets are aligned with its obligations under the **Paris Agreement**, signed in **2015**.
 
• The agreement aims to limit global warming to **below 2°C**, with efforts to restrict it to **1.5°C**.
 
 
 
• **International Solar Alliance (ISA):**
 
 
• Launched by India and France in **2015**, the ISA promotes solar energy deployment in **121 tropical countries**.
 
• It aims to mobilize **$1 trillion** in investments by **2030** for solar energy projects.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy Financing:**
 
 
• India has received funding from international institutions like the **World Bank** and **ADB** for renewable energy projects.
 
• Domestic financing mechanisms like **Renewable Energy Development Fund** and **Viability Gap Funding (VGF)** have supported infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite progress, challenges include **grid integration**, **storage solutions**, and **high initial costs** of renewable projects.
 
• Policies like **Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs)** aim to overcome these issues by mandating power utilities to purchase renewable energy.

questions.question: Which international day was observed for the first time on 12 April 2025, as declared by the United Nations?

options.text: International Day of Human Space Flight
International Day for Dialogue Between Civilizations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**International Day of Human Space Flight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day of Human Space Flight** is observed annually on **12 April** to commemorate the first human space flight.
 
• This day marks the anniversary of the first manned space mission by **Yuri Gagarin**, a Soviet cosmonaut, on **12 April 1961**. This historic event made Yuri Gagarin the first human to travel into outer space.
 
• The United Nations General Assembly declared the observance of this day on **7 April 2011**, through a resolution to recognize the beginning of the space era for humanity.
 
• The day celebrates **human achievements in space exploration** and promotes international cooperation for peaceful uses of outer space.
 
• Yuri Gagarin’s spacecraft, **Vostok 1**, completed one orbit around the Earth in **108 minutes**, a milestone in the history of space exploration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of Human Space Flight:**

 
 
• The space era began with the launch of the first artificial satellite, **Sputnik 1**, by the Soviet Union on **4 October 1957**.
 
• Yuri Gagarin’s historic flight on **12 April 1961** made him an international hero and demonstrated the potential for human space exploration.
 
• His spacecraft, **Vostok 1**, traveled at a speed of around **27,400 km/h**, reaching an altitude of 327 kilometers.
 
• This achievement paved the way for subsequent human space missions, including the **Apollo Moon landings** and the establishment of the **International Space Station (ISS)**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of International Day of Human Space Flight:**
 
 
• The day highlights the significance of **space technology** and its contributions to scientific research, innovation, and global development.
 
• It promotes the peaceful use of outer space and encourages international cooperation in space exploration.
 
• The observance inspires new generations to pursue careers in **science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM)** fields.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Observances:**
 
 
• **World Space Week:** Celebrated annually from **4 to 10 October**, it highlights the benefits of space exploration.
 
• **Moon Day:** Observed on **20 July**, it commemorates the first human Moon landing by Apollo 11 in 1969.
 
 
 
• **Space Exploration Milestones:**
 
 
• **1969:** Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon during NASA’s Apollo 11 mission.
 
• **2001:** Dennis Tito became the first space tourist.
 
• **2021:** The first civilian spaceflight was launched by SpaceX under the Inspiration4 mission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Yuri Gagarin:** He was a Russian pilot and cosmonaut who became the first human to journey into outer space. His flight lasted **108 minutes**.
 
• **Vostok 1:** This spacecraft carried Yuri Gagarin into space. It was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in present-day **Kazakhstan**.
 
• The **United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA)** plays a significant role in promoting international cooperation in space exploration.
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** is an example of global collaboration in space research, involving countries like the USA, Russia, Japan, Canada, and European nations.
 
• The advent of private companies like **SpaceX, Blue Origin,** and **Virgin Galactic** has further revolutionized space travel and exploration.

questions.question: The theme of National Nurses Day 2025 was 'Our Nurses. Our Future. Caring for nurses strengthens economies'. When was this day celebrated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12 May**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Nurses Day** is celebrated annually to honor the contributions of nurses and their pivotal role in healthcare systems.
 
• The theme for **National Nurses Day 2025** was "**Our Nurses. Our Future. Caring for nurses strengthens economies**," emphasizing the importance of nurses in building resilient healthcare systems and driving economic growth.
 
• In **India**, National Nurses Day is celebrated on **May 12** every year. This date coincides with the birth anniversary of **Florence Nightingale**, the founder of modern nursing.
 
• The date mentioned in the question, "**Tue May 12 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**," refers to the observance of National Nurses Day in **India** for the year 2026. Hence, this option is correct.
 
• The event serves as a platform to recognize and appreciate the dedication and selflessness of nurses in improving public health and ensuring patient well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Florence Nightingale:**

 
 
• Born on **12 May 1820**, Florence Nightingale revolutionized nursing practices and established nursing as a professional discipline.
 
• Her work during the **Crimean War** (1853–1856) highlighted the importance of sanitation, hygiene, and patient care in hospitals.
 
• She is often referred to as the "**Lady with the Lamp**" due to her nightly rounds caring for injured soldiers.
 
• Her efforts laid the foundation for modern nursing education and practices worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Nurses Day:**
 
 
• The day is observed globally to recognize the indispensable role nurses play in healthcare delivery and community welfare.
 
• It aims to raise awareness about the challenges faced by nurses and advocate for better working conditions, training, and career opportunities.
 
• Events such as workshops, seminars, and award ceremonies are organized to celebrate the achievements of nurses.
 
 
 
• **Role of Nurses in Healthcare:**
 
 
• Nurses are responsible for patient care, health education, disease prevention, and post-treatment recovery.
 
• They act as intermediaries between patients, doctors, and other healthcare professionals.
 
• During crises such as the **COVID-19 pandemic**, nurses played a critical role in frontline healthcare services.
 
 
 
• **India's Nursing Workforce:**
 
 
• India has a robust nursing workforce, with approximately **3.07 million registered nurses**, according to reports.
 
• The government has implemented various initiatives to improve nursing education, such as establishing nursing colleges and training institutes.
 
• Programs like the **National Health Mission** emphasize the integration of nurses into community healthcare services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Observances Related to Healthcare:**

 
 
• **World Health Day:** Celebrated on **April 7** each year to commemorate the founding of the **World Health Organization** (WHO).
 
• **International Day of the Midwife:** Observed on **May 5**, focusing on the contributions of midwives to maternal and newborn health.
 
• **World Mental Health Day:** Observed on **October 10**, raising awareness about mental health issues and promoting mental well-being.
 
 
 
• **Key Government Initiatives in Nursing:**
 
 
• The **Indian Nursing Council** regulates nursing education and practice in India, ensuring high standards of care and training.

questions.question: The ‘GenomeIndia’ project that has completed whole genome sequencing (WGS) on a database of thousands of individuals in April 2025 was launched in ____.

__
 
• The **GenomeIndia Project** was launched in **2019** by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India.
 
• The primary aim of the project is to create a **genomic database** representing the diverse genetic makeup of the Indian population.
 
• The project involves sequencing the **whole genome (WGS)** of a large number of individuals from across India to better understand the role of genetics in health and disease.
 
• As of **April 2025**, the project has successfully completed whole genome sequencing on a database of **thousands of individuals**.
 
• The GenomeIndia initiative is expected to contribute to **precision medicine**, drug discovery, and healthcare advancements tailored to India's unique genetic diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **GenomeIndia Project Objectives:**

 
 
• To establish a comprehensive **genomic map** of the Indian population by sequencing the genomes of 10,000 individuals.
 
• To enable research in **personalized medicine** and identify genetic markers for diseases common in India, such as diabetes and cardiovascular diseases.
 
• To promote **precision healthcare** by tailoring treatments and therapies based on individual genetic profiles.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Genome Sequencing:**
 
 
• Genome sequencing helps identify **genetic mutations** responsible for diseases, enabling early detection and preventive measures.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **drug development** by targeting specific genetic pathways.
 
• Genome data can aid in studying **ancestry** and population migration patterns.
 
 
 
• **Other Global Genomic Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Human Genome Project** (HGP), completed in 2003, was a global initiative to map all human genes.
 
• The **UK Biobank** is a major resource containing genetic and health data from 500,000 UK participants.
 
• China has launched its **China Precision Medicine Initiative** to sequence genomes of its population for healthcare advancements.
 
 
 
• **GenomeIndia and Diversity:**
 
 
• India is one of the most **genetically diverse** countries, with significant variations across regions, languages, and ethnic groups.
 
• The project aims to bridge gaps in **genomic research** for underrepresented populations in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Genome Sequencing Process:**

 
 
• Genome sequencing involves determining the exact order of the **DNA nucleotides** in an organism.
 
• Technologies like **Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)** and **Sanger Sequencing** are commonly used.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Healthcare:**
 
 
• Genomic data helps in developing **targeted therapies** for cancer and rare genetic disorders.
 
• It is used in **pharmacogenomics** to understand how genes influence drug responses.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Ensuring the **privacy and security** of genomic data is a major concern.
 
• Ethical considerations arise in the use of genetic data for research and healthcare.

questions.question: Which state emerged as India’s first fully literate state, following a major literacy drive under the ULLAS scheme, in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala**, in **May 2025**, emerged as **India’s first fully literate state**, achieving this milestone through the implementation of the **ULLAS scheme**, a major literacy drive aimed at eradicating illiteracy among all age groups.
 
• The **ULLAS scheme** is a state-led initiative that focuses on ensuring literacy among marginalized and disadvantaged communities, including women, tribal groups, and rural populations.
 
• Kerala has historically been a leader in literacy and education in India, with its literacy rate consistently among the highest in the country. The state's literacy rate prior to achieving full literacy was around **96.2% as of the 2011 Census**.
 
• The success of the **ULLAS scheme** was attributed to a collaborative approach involving **government agencies, local self-governing bodies, NGOs, and community volunteers**, ensuring that every individual had access to education.
 
• Kerala's achievement underscores its commitment to **socio-economic development** through education, which serves as a fundamental tool for empowerment and poverty alleviation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ULLAS Scheme:**

 
 
• The **ULLAS scheme** stands for "Unnati Literacy and Learning for All Scheme." It was launched by the Kerala government to eradicate illiteracy and ensure access to education for all citizens in the state.
 
• The program targeted adults who had missed formal education opportunities, focusing on basic literacy, functional literacy, and skill development.
 
• It incorporated innovative teaching methods such as **digital literacy programs**, community learning centers, and mobile learning units to reach remote areas.
 
• The scheme also emphasized the importance of **women's education** as a key to improving family welfare and societal progress.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Historical Literacy Achievements:**
 
 
• Kerala has been a pioneer in education and literacy since the pre-independence era, with significant investments in public education and social reforms.
 
• The state achieved a literacy rate of **90.92% in 1991**, making it the first Indian state to cross the 90% mark.
 
• Kerala's focus on **universal education** was driven by social movements such as the **Vaikom Satyagraha** and the efforts of reformers like **Sree Narayana Guru**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other States:**
 
 
• **Goa:** Goa has a high literacy rate but has not achieved full literacy. Its literacy rate was **87% as per the 2011 Census**.
 
• **Mizoram:** Mizoram is among the northeastern states with a commendable literacy rate of **91.58% (2011 Census)**, but it remains below Kerala’s achievement.
 
• **Gujarat:** Gujarat has made significant strides in literacy, with a rate of **78.03% in 2011**, but it is not close to achieving full literacy.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Literacy:**
 
 
• Literacy is a vital tool for **socio-economic development**, enabling individuals to access better employment opportunities, healthcare, and civic participation.
 
• Kerala's literacy achievement has resulted in improved **human development indices**, including higher life expectancy, lower infant mortality, and better gender equality.
 
• Full literacy contributes to **poverty alleviation** by empowering individuals with knowledge and skills to improve their livelihoods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kerala's Education Policies:**

 
 
• Kerala has implemented robust policies to promote education, such as the **Right to Education Act** and state-sponsored literacy programs.
 
• The state's investment in **public education infrastructure**, including libraries, schools, and community centers, has played a significant role in achieving full literacy.
 
• Kerala’s focus on **inclusive education** ensures that marginalized groups, including tribal communities and women, have equal access to educational resources.
 
 
 
• **National Context:**
 
 
• India’s overall literacy rate was **74.04% as per the 2011 Census**, with significant disparities between states and genders.
 
• Efforts like the **National Literacy Mission (1988)** and **Saakshar Bharat Program (2009)** have contributed to improving literacy rates nationwide.
 
• Kerala’s achievement serves as a model for other states to implement similar initiatives to bridge literacy gaps.

questions.question: The National Florence Nightingale Awards, conferred by the President of India in May 2025, are given to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nursing professionals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Florence Nightingale Awards** are prestigious awards conferred by the **President of India** to honor excellence in the field of **nursing services**. This recognition was established to commemorate the contributions of **Florence Nightingale**, known as the "Lady with the Lamp" and the founder of modern nursing.
 
• The awards are presented annually on **International Nurses Day (May 12)**, which marks the birth anniversary of Florence Nightingale. These awards aim to acknowledge the exemplary work done by **nursing professionals** in public health and patient care.
 
• The recipients of these awards include **nurses** working in various sectors like government hospitals, private healthcare facilities, community health, and other healthcare institutions across India.
 
• The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare plays a pivotal role in organizing the awards. The selection process involves a rigorous evaluation of nominations sent by state governments, union territories, and institutions based on the **nurses' contributions and dedication** to healthcare.
 
• The awards include a **medal, a certificate, and a monetary award** as a token of appreciation for their invaluable services to society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Florence Nightingale:**

 
 
• Florence Nightingale (1820–1910) was an English social reformer and founder of modern nursing. She gained prominence during the **Crimean War** (1853–1856) for her work in improving sanitation and reducing mortality rates in war hospitals.
 
• Her efforts revolutionized healthcare practices and established nursing as a professional career.
 
• The **Florence Nightingale Pledge**, often recited by nurses, emphasizes dedication, ethics, and compassion in nursing practice.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Nursing Professionals:**
 
 
• **Nurses** form the backbone of the healthcare system by delivering direct patient care, assisting in surgeries, and managing critical care units.
 
• They play a crucial role in promoting public health initiatives, such as immunization drives, maternal and child health programs, and disease prevention campaigns.
 
• During the **COVID-19 pandemic**, nurses worldwide demonstrated extraordinary courage and resilience in combating the crisis, often working under challenging conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Healthcare Awards in India:**
 
 
• The **Padma Awards** (Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan) also recognize individuals for their exceptional contributions to **medicine and healthcare**.
 
• The **Dr. B.C. Roy National Award** is another prominent recognition given to doctors for their excellence in the field of medicine.
 
• The **Ayushman Bharat Health Awards** are conferred to healthcare professionals and institutions contributing to the success of the **Ayushman Bharat Scheme**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **Indian Nursing Council** (INC), established in **1947**, regulates nursing education and practices in India, ensuring quality standards are maintained.
 
• India faces a challenge in terms of the **nurse-to-patient ratio**, which is below the World Health Organization's recommended standards of 1 nurse per 300 patients.
 
• Efforts are being made by the government to improve nursing education and infrastructure through initiatives like the **Skill India Mission** and the establishment of new nursing colleges across the country.

questions.question: The Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the National Referral Centre for Wildlife in which city in 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• In **2025**, the **Prime Minister of India** laid the **foundation stone** for the **National Referral Centre for Wildlife** in **Junagadh, Gujarat**.
 
• The centre is being established to strengthen **wildlife health management**, **advanced veterinary care**, and **disease diagnosis** for wild animals.
 
• It will function as a **specialised national-level facility** to handle complex wildlife cases and provide expert support to wildlife veterinarians across the country.
 
• The facility is strategically located near the **Gir landscape**, which is the only natural habitat of the **Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica)**.
 
• The centre will contribute to strengthening India’s **wildlife conservation infrastructure**, research, and capacity building in **wildlife medicine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary**

 
 
• Located in **Gujarat**, near **Junagadh** and **Gir Somnath districts**.
 
• It is the **only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion** in the world.
 
• Established as a **wildlife sanctuary in 1965**.
 
 
 
• **Asiatic Lion**

• **Wildlife Conservation in India**
 
 
• Governed under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• India has more than **100 national parks** and over **500 wildlife sanctuaries**.
